Description
Living World
Here you will find NPCs all over the world, narrators who decide your fate, a living world that changes as time goes on, NPCs who live their own lives, base management and, very important, NPCs who drive for you: do what you need to do while the NPC does their job.
Other survivors share the map with you. They have needs, they work, they get hurt, and they remember how you treated them. Some will join you. Most have their own people and their own plans.

Quick answers
Which version does it run on?
Build 42.21/42.22 or later.
Does it work on servers?
Not yet. Single player only for now.
Can I add it to a save I already have?
Yes. The first time it runs, it places a few communities, a bandit base and some people living alone in buildings around the map. More people arrive over time.
Can I remove it later?
Yes, the save still opens. The NPCs are gone while the mod is off, and they come back as they were when you turn it on again. What they built stays either way.
Will it slow my game down?
No. The mod is optimized to run well even with 100 NPCs around you.
Do NPCs come back as zombies when I load?
No.
Which languages?
English, Brazilian Portuguese, Spanish, Russian and Chinese.
Where are the settings?
Keys and what shows on screen are in Options -> Mods. How many communities and bandit bases there are, and how often things happen, is in the sandbox options.
How do I learn to use the mod?
Open the Management window (button on the left sidebar, or the "." key) and press Help. Every mechanic is explained there, with pictures.

What you can do
  • Pick one of four narrators. The narrator decides how often trouble finds you, and has a word with you now and then.
  • Invite people to your team, trade for their help, and give them orders: follow me, stay here, come here, run with me.
  • Put them to work at your base: cooking, farming, animals, fishing, traps, hunting, fuel for the generator, car repair, sewing, building, barricades, guard duty and dealing with corpses. Each job has its own priority.
  • Mark zones and storage rules, and ask for new buildings with "Build here".
  • Send them to loot a building or patrol points on the map, and keep in touch by walkie-talkie.
  • Let a team member drive, or have them follow your car.
  • Trade with other communities, pay for their services, or help them when they ask.
  • Deal with bandits: pay up, haggle, buy a truce, rescue a prisoner, fight or run.
  • Make your own NPCs with the NPC creator in the main menu.

What the NPCs do
  • Eat, drink, sleep, get cold and wet, and carry real items with real weight.
  • Get hurt, bandage each other and get infected. A bite in the team is your call.
  • Fight with their own weapons, push and stomp, shoot, and run when it gets bad.
  • Move carefully outside: crouch, peek, open and close doors, climb fences and windows, use a flashlight at night.
  • Have a personality, a job from before, a home and a few things they will not give up.
  • Talk, make friends and grudges, get bored and grieve. Someone unhappy and greedy may rob your storage and leave.
  • Get better at what they do.

The world keeps going
  • Communities have a name, a color, a leader and their own stock. Their bases grow from a few barricades into a fortress, wear down and fall.
  • They send expeditions, visit their neighbors, talk on the radio and fight each other. Leaders get challenged and groups split.
  • New people arrive over time. Some live alone, some drive around.
  • Things happen away from you, and you find what is left. The news and the "Survivors" radio channel tell you about it.
  • Bandits, military, police and cults.

Works with
  • Companion Dogs

Planned
  • Multiplayer.
  • Integration and testing with other popular mods.
  • An API so other mods can build on this one.
  • Better interactions with the NPCs.
  • Optional AI integration, for anyone who wants a more dynamic experience.

Known issues
  • Single player only. Multiplayer does not work yet.
  • Not tested with other mods. Mods that change zombies, or that treat NPCs as zombies, may not work well with it. If something breaks with another mod, say which one in the comments.
  • A team member driving on a long trip sometimes gets stuck at the end of a dead-end street.
  • Long car trips plan their way on the streets of the vanilla map. Streets added by map mods are not part of the full route.
  • The Spanish, Russian and Chinese texts have not been checked by native speakers yet. In Chinese, some characters show in traditional form, because the game's font does not have the simplified ones.
  • The Help pictures are in English and Portuguese. Other languages show the English ones.

I know this is a new mod so I just want to say great work on the stability of it! The main issue I noticed is that NPCs walk around erratically and quickly, often ignoring zombies or hostile NPCs. It seems their priorities aren't focused on getting rid of danger.

Sometimes they'll walk up to a zombie and just stand there, hit them once, walk away, get hit, walk away, etc. Same thing when they have a gun.

Overall I think your focus for improvement should be on making the NPCs move and fight more naturally. I hate to keep bringing up the comparison but, Project A Life has a pretty good system, whatever it is, for how the NPCs move and fight.


The interaction system in your mod is great, but the way that NPCs currently behave and move makes me want to wait for more polish on it. What are your plans for that? Maybe you and Vice can collaborate.

A Life's NPC behavior with your interface/interaction menu would be the ultimate system. Anyhow, great job so far!
